gamespot.com/articles/get-the-entire-met.title: Get The Entire Metro Series For Under $9 Ahead Of Metro 2039’s Release
gamespot.com/articles/get-the-entire-met.excerpt: While I’m a fan of the Stalker games, there’s something about the more linear nature and, ironically, on-rails experience that the Metro games deliver. With a tense atmosphere, mutated creatures, and factions split within the underground of a demolished Russia, the Metro series might be some of my favorite FPS games of all time—and with Metro 2039 almost here, now’s the chance to catch up on the series for less than $9. That’s all three of the games released so far. The series starts with Metro 2033 , two decades after an apocalyptic event ended most of mankind and turned the surface into a radioactive wasteland. Even breathing the air is enough to kill you, but the monstrous creatures above will do that far quicker. You play as Artyom, who leaves the safety of his home station in order to warn the rest of the metro about a new, mysterious mutant threat called the Dark Ones. I can’t really go into more detail on Metro Last Light without spoiling the predecessor. So, just take my word for it: it is arguably better, with a great narrative bolstered by gameplay improvements. Metro Exodus follows Artyom as he believes life still continues outside of Moscow, and aboard the Aurora train alongside his wife and the Spartan Rangers, he heads off to discover the truth. In all three of the Metro games, you’re limited to a first-person view, putting you face-to-face with enemies of the human and mutant variety. Even though it may look like your typical FPS game, there’s a lot more of a survival focus, with limited resources meaning that every bullet needs to count, and using your gas mask’s filters at the right time is essential to surviving. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bKY_Ks_VG9Q All three Metro games are the remastered or enhanced editions with this discount. In fact, Exodus is actually the version that includes all post-launch DLC, so you’re getting the entire Metro series so far at a very steep discount, right as the Metro 2039 release date has been announced. gamespot.com/articles/see-the-ripped-gam.title: See Ripped Game Of Thrones Actor’s Pitch To Play God Of War’s Kratos In Role Already Cast By Another Ripped Actor
gamespot.com/articles/see-the-ripped-gam.excerpt: God of War fans have been on a rollercoaster ride recently while waiting for the TV show adaptation to come to life. After originally casting Ryan Hurst for the role, Amazon was forced to find another suitably ripped actor after Hurst was horrifically injured on set. Last week his replacement, Dave Bautista, showed off his transformation so far for the role. Now, though, Game of Thrones actor Hafþór Júlíus Björnsson, or Thor Bjornsson, who played The Mountain in the HBO series, has shared an image depicting him as Kratos, asking fans if they'd like to see him take on the role. https://twitter.com/ThorBjornsson_/status/2096705259036946858?s=20 Posting on X , Bjornsson captioned the image, "Be honest... would you guys want to see me as Kratos?" The image, likely generated by AI, shows the ripped actor in an even more ripped state, dressed in Kratos' attire, complete with his trademark red tattoo, inked to honor his brother, Deimos. Of course, with Bautista already cast, Bjornsson's desire to portray Kratos is merely a wish, and isn't likely to come to fruition, but it's fun to see the towering 6 foot 9 Icelandic strongman looking like a Spartan warrior. Several other actors have expressed a desire to play the role, including Christopher Judge, the game's original voice actor. However, he's pretty frustrated that TV show adaptations regularly fail to hire anyone that worked on the source material. The God of War TV show is expected to resume production in late October or early November, although there's no estimated release date for the series just yet.

gamespot.com/articles/the-weirdest-world.title: The Weirdest Worlds That Could Technically Be In Kingdom Hearts 4
gamespot.com/articles/the-weirdest-world.excerpt: Over the past couple weeks, we've finally learned a bit more about the next entry in Square Enix's Kingdom Hearts series. In an extended Kingdom Hearts 4 trailer revealed during D23 , Disney's annual fan event, we were given a first look at Coco's Land of The Dead, and its narrative implications already have us speculating as to what worlds could come next . But while pondering what worlds could realistically be in Kingdom Hearts 4 is fun, you know what's even better? Thinking about all of the world that could technically be in Kingdom Hearts 4, with no regards to how absolutely baffling their inclusion might be. In the years since the Kingdom Hearts series first began, Disney has flexed its mouse money and purchased a lot of various companies and properties, and though you're probably well aware that Disney owns both Marvel and Star Wars, that's just scratching the surface of everything Mickey Mouse has gobbled up. Naturally, having access to all of these properties means that Disney could include them in Kingdom Hearts, so here are some of the weirdest places we could (but probably won't) go to in Sora's next adventure. Pandora (Avatar) Though I can imagine a world in which Sora joins up with Aang, Katara, and the gang, we're talking about the blue Avatar here. Sure, James Cameron still owns the creative rights to his sprawling sci-fi franchise, but Disney's merger with 20th Century Fox gave the company both distribution and merchandising rights to Avatar, as well as the ability to use the property so long as Cameron gives his permission. The ball is in your court, Jim. -- Jessica Cogswell Philadelphia (It's Always Sunny In Philadelphia) Having already crossed over with Abbott Elementary, It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia has already shown it can be brought over into a less R-rated world. Seeing the gang turned into an RPG party feels like a golden opportunity for some comedy, though the mature nature of the source material probably makes this an unlikely one. --

After two successful and highly regarded arcade racing games in the Hot Wheels Unleashed series, developer Milestone has taken that same formula and applied it across an open world structure in Hot Wheels: Infinite Rush — an addition that feels unnecessary.
